records.subject: Anatomy
records.stem: ww A71 year old man walks into ED following a fall. He is complaining of neck pain and weakness affecting his upper limbs only. Which of the following spinal cord lesions is most likely:
options: Complete cord transection (x) Brown-Sequard syndrome 4% Vv) Central cord syndrome 28%
records.explanation: Central cord syndrome (CCS) is marked by a disproportionately greater impairment of motor function in the upper extremities than in the lower ones, as well as by bladder dysfunction and a variable amount of sensory loss below the injury level. Vv Spinal Cord Tracts

records.subject: Anatomy
records.stem: ww The primary auditory cortex is located in which of the following regions:
records.explanation: The primary auditory cortex is located in the temporal lobe. The primary auditory cortex and auditory association area are important for perception and recognition of auditory stimuli. v Temporal Lobe ANATOMY / CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM

records.subject: Anatomy
records.stem: ww The primary somatosensory cortex is located in which of the following regions:
records.explanation: The primary somatosensory cortex is located in the postcentral gyrus of the parietal lobe and is concerned with perceiving complex somatosensory stimuli from the contralateral side of the face and body. Together with the somatosensory association cortex, these areas are responsible for sensation and proprioception, and visuo-spatial perception. ; Vv Parietal Lobe ANATOMY / CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM

records.subject: Anatomy
records.stem: ww Which of the following best describes the position of the frontal lobe:
options: Anterior to the parieto-occipital sulcus (Vv) Anterior to the central sulcus and superior to the lateral sulcus 46%
Posterior to the central sulcus and superior to the lateral sulcus
Anterior to the central sulcus and inferior to the lateral sulcus
Posterior to the central sulcus and inferior to the lateral sulcus
records.explanation: The frontal lobe extends from the central sulcus to the frontal pole and lies anterior to the central sulcus and superior to the lateral sulcus. . Vv Frontal Lobe ANATOMY / CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM

Posterior to the central sulcus and inferior to the lateral sulcus

records.explanation: The blood supply to the frontal lobe is from the anterior cerebral artery (supplying the medial surface of the primary motor cortex which controls the lower limb) and the middle cerebral artery (supplying the lateral surface of the primary motor cortex which controls the face and upper limb). : Vv Frontal Lobe ANATOMY / CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM

records.subject: Anatomy
records.stem: pit. A 69 year old patient is brought to ED with acute onset facial weakness on the right side, and difficulty with speech. He is able to respond to questions appropriately by nodding or shaking his head, but his words are jumbled and don't make sense. Which of the following lobes has been affected:
options: Left temporal lobe () Lett frontal lobe 30%
records.explanation: Right sided facial weakness and expressive dysphasia is most likely caused by a lesion to the left frontal lobe, due to damage to the primary motor cortex and the Broca speech area respectively. Vv Frontal Lobe
